task: Analyze synthetic SXS binary black hole numerical-relativity waveform uncertainty datasets for catalog accuracy and coverage claims.
input_data: data/fig6_data.csv: 1500 catalog-wide waveform differences between two highest numerical resolutions after minimal time/phase alignment
data/fig7_data.csv: 1500 x 7 mode-decomposed waveform differences for spherical-harmonic ell=2..8
data/fig8_data.csv: 1200 paired extrapolation-order waveform differences, N=2 vs N=3 and N=2 vs N=4
scientific_commitments: Quantify numerical-resolution waveform uncertainty distribution and long-tail behavior.
Quantify mode-dependent accuracy across ell=2..8 without collapsing the named modal structure.
Quantify extrapolation-order consistency and paired differences between N2-N3 and N2-N4 comparisons.
Compare synthetic data summaries to values stated in the task and related SXS catalog context where available.
Produce reproducible figures and saved source tables supporting all main claims.
named_methods_or_protocols: minimal time and phase alignment waveform difference
primary_target_quantities: median, mean, standard deviation, quantiles, min/max of mismatch-like waveform differences
mode-wise median and quantile scaling with ell
paired ratio and log10 difference for N2-N4 versus N2-N3 extrapolation differences
limitations: Available datasets contain synthetic uncertainty summaries only, not raw strain, Weyl scalar, horizon trajectories, or metadata; analysis therefore evaluates catalog-accuracy diagnostics rather than generating numerical-relativity waveforms.
related_work_updates: Use highest-versus-second-highest resolution comparison as a conservative NR error diagnostic.
Emphasize mode-resolved summaries because higher harmonics and mode mixing are scientifically relevant.
Include thresholds near 1e-3 and 1e-2 motivated by surrogate-model mismatch accuracy discussions.
